newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Red cross truck tests rebel-held southern Albania.
newsitem.headline: Red cross truck tests rebel-held southern Albania.

text.p: A Red Cross truck carrying emergency food to Albania left northern Greece on Thursday in the first attempt to bring humanitarian relief by road through the rebel-held south of Europe's poorest nation.
"The truck left Ioannina in northern Greece this morning headed for Albania," said Alain Lennartz, Swiss head of the International Committee of the Red Cross delegation in Tirana.

The truck, carrying nine tonnes of flour, rice, pasta, sugar, salt and soap, was attempting to resupply hospitals, orphanages and old people's homes in southern towns, seized by armed gangs in a revolt against the Tirana government.
"This is the very first attempt" to resupply Albania by land after the crisis, he told Reuters. "We talked to everybody about it in the local authorities in advance."

There were no plans to seek any police or local armed escorts for the truck through the south, hit by an insurrection this month. The truck was at the border and ready to cross at midday, border officials said.

The truck aimed to travel through the rebel-held southern towns of Gjirokaster, Tepelene and end in the government-held town of Fier on Thursday. On Friday it would travel north to Tirana via Elbasan and end in the port of Durres on Saturday.
"We hope it will go well but we have been concerned about tensions around Gjirokaster," Lennartz said. Gjirokaster is about 30 kms (20 miles) from the Greek border.

Foreign nations have flown aid into Tirana in recent days and Greece has shipped supplies to the port of Sarande. But relief efforts have shied from resupplying southern Albania by land because the area is almost entirely in the hands of rebels.
European relief experts met Prime Minister Bashkim Fino on Thursday to discuss ways of resupplying the country, including a foreign security force to protect shipments from the looting.
The European Union estimates Albania needs 10,000 tonnes of flour and $10 million of medical supplies.

Southern Albania descended into chaos earlier this month after protests over the collapse of popular savings schemes in January that swallowed the savings of thousands of Albanians. More than 100 people have died.
